projects.name: InCloseMail
projects.description: Desktop email that works like classic Outlook, for Microsoft 365 and Outlook.com.
projects.tagline: An Outlook alternative built for the desktop.
projects.featureText: Mail, calendar, people and tasks laid out like classic Outlook, plus AI agents, Clean Up My Inbox and offline mail during Microsoft 365 outages. Free for personal email, with paid plans for business accounts.
projects.longDescription:
InCloseMail works like classic Outlook, screen by screen: the ribbon, folder pane, reading pane and To-Do Bar, Outlook's keyboard shortcuts and right-click menus, .pst import and export, Focused Inbox, server-side rules and Quick Steps, S/MIME signed and encrypted mail, and a calendar with the Scheduling Assistant, Room Finder and Teams meetings. People, Microsoft To Do tasks, shared mailboxes with Send As, aliases, Microsoft 365 Groups and profiles are all there, and settings and signatures follow you to other PCs.

It adds things Outlook doesn't have. AI agents such as Claude (Claude Code connects in one click) can read, translate and draft mail in the mailboxes you choose, and anything they propose changes nothing until you click Apply. Clean Up My Inbox groups likely junk, newsletters, people you never answer and big old messages so you can act on thousands at once, with one Undo. You can remap any keyboard shortcut, run rules on folders of any size, blacklist a sender on every device in one click, see why a message looks suspicious, and get a second look before sending to outside recipients or forgetting an attachment.

There is also Analytics about your own mail (kept on your PC), Lock InCloseMail with Windows Hello, read-only accounts, Dark Mode that darkens emailed charts, themes and a Theme Editor, sticky Notes shared across your PCs, RSS feeds and a Demo Mode with a sample mailbox. It keeps working offline during a Microsoft 365 outage, and comes in ten languages. IT gets a signed MSI with Group Policy and Intune templates.

It is free forever for Outlook.com, Hotmail, Live and other personal Microsoft accounts. Microsoft 365 work accounts will cost $3 per user per month ($36 a year) after the beta, and are free during it; one licence covers one person on up to three PCs. The first public beta, version 26.11.2608, came out on November 26, 2026. It runs on 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later) and Windows 11.

projects.name: DesktopWiki
projects.description: A private wiki and password manager for a family or small team, running on your own Windows PC.
projects.tagline: A team wiki that runs on your own PC.
projects.featureText: Spaces, a page tree and a visual editor, plus a shared password manager, a family start page and home network monitoring, with no server or cloud account to set up. Free for one person, with paid plans for families and teams.
projects.longDescription:
DesktopWiki gives a family or small team a private wiki the way classic team wikis work: spaces with a page tree, a visual editor, templates, labels, comments and @mentions, page history with compare and restore, and search that reaches inside PDFs and scanned files. It also has databases with table, board, card and timeline views, whiteboards, diagrams, slides, per-space blogs, approvals, rules, a family calendar, chores with stars and rewards, and export to Word, Markdown or PDF. You install it on one Windows PC, and everyone else opens it in a browser on a phone or another computer.

It includes a password manager with private and shared vaults (AES-256 and Argon2id), built-in two-step codes, password health checks, emergency access, sharing by link, and import from 1Password, Bitwarden, LastPass, KeePass, Dashlane and browsers. A personal start page brings links, weather, news, countdowns, to-dos and a wall display mode for a tablet. Home network monitoring checks your devices and internet, tells router, line and DNS faults apart, and tracks screen time on kids' PCs, consoles and TVs.

There is no server, database or cloud account to set up: the whole wiki lives in one file you can back up by copying it, and it does encrypted daily or weekly backups too. It can import Confluence spaces and whole-site backups, plus Word, spreadsheets, Markdown and web pages. A free desktopwiki.net address, Tailscale or port forwarding can open it up for use away from home. It comes in nine languages, and AI agents can connect with read-only access.

It is free for one person. Family (up to 6 people) is $49 a year, Team (up to 18) $99 and Business (up to 60) $199, on sale after the beta ends on December 31, 2026, with every feature in every plan. Everyone who ran the beta gets their first year of Family free. The host PC needs 64-bit Windows 10 (version 1809 or later), Windows 11 or Windows Server 2019 or later.

projects.name: macshot
projects.alternative: Alternative to the macOS screenshot tool
projects.description: Capture, annotate, and record your screen. Includes scrolling capture and text recognition.
projects.longDescription:
macshot lives in the Mac menu bar. One hotkey freezes the screen so you can select a region, mark it up with arrows, text, shapes, numbered markers or blur, and copy it straight to the clipboard.

It also records the screen as MP4 or GIF with system audio and microphone, stitches scrolling captures into one tall image, reads text with OCR, can auto-redact emails, phone numbers and card numbers, and uploads to Google Drive, imgbb or any S3-compatible storage. It is a native Swift and AppKit app, also installable with Homebrew (brew install --cask macshot).
projects.builtWithAI: The macshot repo includes CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md instruction files for AI coding agents, and its commit history shows AI help: 37 of its 1,052 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude and 5 by Cursor. Most of the code is credited to its developer, sw33tLie.

projects.name: Locode
projects.description: Build React web apps from prompts using local Ollama models on an Apple Silicon Mac.
projects.longDescription:
Describe an app in plain English and Locode generates a complete React, Tailwind and Vite project, tests it with Playwright, fixes errors and lets you keep refining it with follow-up prompts. Everything runs on your own machine through Ollama, so there are no API keys or subscriptions.

The ready-made download is a DMG for Apple Silicon Macs. It can also be run from source with Python and Node.

projects.name: Glance
projects.description: Host and share previews of pages built by coding agents like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor.
projects.longDescription:
Glance lets a coding agent publish a page, dashboard or app to a live URL with one command (glance deploy). You leave comments on the page in the browser, much like in a Google Doc, and the agent reads them and fixes the page.

You host it yourself on Cloudflare's free tier. It works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Cline, Aider or any agent that can run a shell command, every link needs a login, and optional Slack notifications tell you about new comments.
projects.builtWithAI: Glance's commit history shows it was built mostly with Claude: 206 of its 251 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude models.

projects.name: FreeFlow
projects.description: Free voice dictation for your computer. Speak and it types for you, with no monthly subscription.
projects.builtWithAI: Zach Latta's original README (February 2026) said he "vibe-coded" FreeFlow over a weekend. The project keeps an AGENTS.md file for AI coding agents, and 97 of its 511 commits (checked 2026-11-21) are co-authored by Claude.
projects.longDescription:
Hold the Fn key, talk, and FreeFlow types what you said into whatever text field you are in. It cleans up filler words and spelling using nearby app context and your own vocabulary list, and Edit Mode can rewrite selected text from a spoken instruction such as "make this shorter".

It uses a free Groq API key by default, or any OpenAI-compatible provider including local models through Ollama or LM Studio. There is no FreeFlow server. It works on Apple Silicon and Intel Macs.

whatPeopleSay.summary: FreeFlow got a well-received Show HN launch, where people liked having a free alternative to paid dictation apps such as Wispr Flow and Superwhisper. Commenters pointed out that it only runs on macOS and that it sends audio to a cloud model rather than transcribing on the device, and many used the thread to compare it with local tools like Handy. Beyond that thread and a short positive write-up, coverage is thin.
praise: Free, with no monthly subscription, unlike the paid tools it replaces
Fast enough that dictation does not interrupt your work
Open source
complaints: Only works on macOS
Uses a cloud model instead of transcribing locally, which some saw as a privacy trade-off
Some commenters preferred fully local alternatives such as Handy

projects.name: Open Source Barware
projects.alternative: Alternative to paid bar inventory software
projects.description: Local-first bar inventory software for counting stock and tracking usage, licensed GPLv3.
projects.longDescription:
Walk your shelves and say what you see ("Tito's, half. Jameson, full.") and Open Source Barware builds the count sheet, prices every bottle and tells you what's short and what to reorder. Import last week's sales from your POS and it flags bottles that came up short.

It runs on your own Mac or Windows laptop, works without internet or AI (AI is optional, for reading invoice photos), counts in English or Spanish and can run several locations. There is a sample bar to try in the browser. It is free with no paid tier, under GPLv3.
projects.builtWithAI: The maker says AI is what let people from the bar trade build the tool themselves. The GitHub repo keeps CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md files for AI coding agents, and 56 of its 249 commits (checked 2026-11-22) are co-authored by Claude.

whatPeopleSay.summary: Most of the discussion comes from one Hacker News thread, and it was largely skeptical. Some commenters saw it as a possible free alternative to paid bar inventory services. Others questioned why invoice reading needs a cloud AI, called it a thin layer over a spreadsheet, and said the polished, AI-written website made the project harder to trust. A Product Hunt launch drew only a handful of upvotes and one positive comment.
praise: Could replace paid bar inventory subscriptions
Local-first design, with the cloud used only for reading invoice photos
Interface looks polished
complaints: Uses cloud AI for invoice reading when local OCR could do the job
Seen by some as a spreadsheet with an opinionated front end
Marketing site felt AI-generated and short on a plain description of what the program does
No iPad or mobile app for counting stock behind the bar

projects.longDescription:

projects.description: A free 2D and 3D CAD app with the command line, snaps, layers and dimensions drafters know, reading and writing DXF and DWG, for Windows, Mac, Linux, FreeBSD and the web, from the ArtCraft suite. Early development.
projects.longDescription:
CADCraft follows the classic drafting workflow: type a command such as LINE, click points or enter coordinates, and use object snaps, polar tracking, ortho, grips and right-click to repeat. projects.name: TextureCraft
projects.description: A free 3D texture painting app with layers, masks, smart materials and GPU mesh-map baking, for Windows, Mac, Linux, FreeBSD and the web, from the ArtCraft suite. In active development.
projects.longDescription:
TextureCraft paints PBR materials straight onto 3D models in a layer stack with masks, generators and smart materials. Brush strokes flow across UV seams, mesh maps bake on the GPU, and a path-traced Rendering mode previews the result.

It imports glTF/GLB, FBX, COLLADA, USD, Alembic, OBJ, PLY and STL, and exports textures as PNG, JPEG, TGA, TIFF, EXR, HDR and more at 8, 16 or 32 bits with UDIM tiles. Materials from MaterialCraft can be sent straight to its shelf. Its README (2026-11-01) estimates about 93% of a texture artist's daily workflow works end to end.

projects.name: Clean Your TV
projects.alternative: Alternative to the stock Google TV home screen
projects.description: Strips the ads, tracking and preloaded bloat from an Android TV or Google TV over Wi-Fi and swaps in a clean, Apple TV-style home screen. No root, nothing uninstalled, and one command undoes it all.
projects.longDescription:
Android TVs have the same debug bridge as Android phones. Clean Your TV uses it over Wi-Fi to back up your settings, switch off the maker's telemetry, ad services, sponsored rows and preloaded apps (switched off, not deleted), and install a small native launcher as the home screen. Its lists cover 504 TV models from 138 brands.

The usual way to run it is to hand the project's prompt to a coding assistant such as Claude Code, Codex or Gemini CLI on a computer on the same Wi-Fi; it finds the bloat on your TV and asks before touching anything you might use. You can also run the same steps by hand. There is no app-store app and no prebuilt APK. Samsung, LG, Roku, Vizio and Hisense VIDAA TVs are not supported.

It started on 17 October 2026 as a before-and-after post of the maker's parents' TV that reached 8.6M views. It was the #1 trending repository on GitHub for the week of 19 to 25 October and had about 60,000 stars by late November, with coverage in TechCrunch, TechRadar, Tom's Guide, Android Authority, XDA and hundreds more.
projects.builtWithAI: The maker says the first TV was "cleaned up by Claude Code over Wi-Fi", and the project is designed to be run by a coding assistant. Checked 2026-11-22 in the repo's commit history: 1,136 of 6,869 commits are co-authored by Claude, and the repo has an AGENTS.md file.

It is in the App Store, Google Play and Flathub, with downloads for Windows and Linux and a web version. The app is free; optional Plus ($4.99 a month) and Pro ($9.99 a month) plans add more cloud sync storage, more AI translations and DeepL Pro.

projects.name: Bitchat
projects.description: Jack Dorsey's peer-to-peer messenger that works without the internet over a Bluetooth mesh, and over Nostr relays when you are online. No accounts, no phone numbers, no servers.
projects.longDescription:
Nearby phones relay messages to each other over Bluetooth Low Energy, up to seven hops, so a group can keep chatting at a protest, a festival or after a disaster with no signal. When you are online it reaches further through Nostr relays, including location channels for your block, neighbourhood or city. Private messages are end-to-end encrypted with the Noise protocol, and a triple tap wipes everything.

The iPhone and Mac app is in the App Store, and the Android app is on Google Play and GitHub. It launched in July 2025 and has had wide press coverage; Dorsey has said it had no external security review at launch.
projects.builtWithAI: Business Insider (July 2025) reported that Dorsey built it as a weekend project with Block's AI coding agent Goose ("It worked within a day"). Checked 2026-11-22 in the commit history: 201 of 1,088 commits in the iOS and Mac repo and 53 of 986 in the Android repo are co-authored by Claude.

whatPeopleSay.summary:
People like the idea behind Bitchat: a messenger with no account or phone number that works offline over a Bluetooth mesh. Commenters keep pointing to censorship, internet shutdowns and disasters as where it matters, and App Store users rate it highly for having no sign-up and no ads. The launch in July 2025 drew sharp criticism from security researchers, who showed that contacts could be impersonated. Dorsey added a warning not to rely on its security, and Trail of Bits, while crediting the quick fixes and the move to the Noise protocol, advised against using it for sensitive conversations at that time.

In everyday use, the common complaints are short Bluetooth range and too few people nearby to form a mesh. Some also worry about battery drain.

Worries about battery drain and reliability over many hops

projects.name: Inbox Zero
projects.description: An AI email assistant for Gmail and Outlook that sorts your inbox, pre-drafts replies in your style and bulk-unsubscribes, plus a fast email client. Self-host it free or use the hosted service.
projects.longDescription:
The assistant works in the background on your Gmail or Outlook account. You tell it in plain English how to handle mail, and it labels and files messages, drafts replies in your tone, tracks what you still need to answer, blocks cold emails, bulk-archives and unsubscribes, briefs you before meetings and saves attachments to Google Drive or OneDrive. You can also chat with it from Slack or Telegram.

The separate email client has a split inbox and all your accounts in one place, on the web and desktop, with iPhone and Android apps. You can self-host it with Docker or use the hosted version at getinboxzero.com.

whatPeopleSay.summary:
There's less independent user discussion of Inbox Zero than its GitHub popularity suggests. The main real conversation is its December 2023 Show HN thread; most of the rest is Product Hunt launch comments and short review-site ratings. People like writing email rules in plain English, the pre-drafted replies, and how fast bulk unsubscribe clears an old inbox, and they value that it's open source and can be self-hosted. projects.name: Voicebox
projects.alternative: Alternative to ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow
projects.description: A local AI voice studio: clone a voice from a few seconds of audio, generate speech in 23 languages, and dictate into any app with a hotkey. Everything runs on your own computer.
projects.longDescription:

It has eight text-to-speech engines, zero-shot voice cloning and 50+ preset voices, effects such as pitch, reverb and compression, and no length limit. Models and voice data never leave your machine. There are installers for Apple silicon and Intel Macs and for Windows; Linux users build from source.

projects.description: A gym and body-weight tracker you host yourself: plan routines, log every set and watch your progress, synced across your phone and laptop.

Notes stay as .md files in a plain folder, with wikilinks and backlinks, and each folder can sync encrypted through iCloud Drive, OneDrive, WebDAV, S3 or Git. One export window writes PDF, Word, HTML, EPUB, LaTeX, ODT, RTF and plain text.

It is a small app (about 14 MB on Windows), free and MIT-licensed, with no account or subscription. Optional AI features work with local models such as Ollama or your own API keys.

projects.name: TelltaleDNS
projects.description: A small, fast DNS server and ad blocker for your home network that shows which device asked for what and why each answer was given. Runs on a Raspberry Pi or any Linux machine.
projects.longDescription:
Every query in the log is tied to a named device and explained. Set blocklists, schedules, safe search and blocked services per device or group, and preview what a change would have done to yesterday's traffic before saving it. It supports encrypted DNS (DoT, DoH, DoQ) both ways, DNSSEC and full recursion.

It is one static binary of about 13 MB that idles at around 14 MB of memory, for amd64, arm64 and 32-bit Pi OS. Install it with a script on any systemd Linux box or run it in Docker; a Pi and Kubernetes nodes can share one config.

projects.description: A complete classic-style online role-playing game you can play free in your browser or in desktop and phone apps: nine classes, quests, dungeons, raids and ranked PvP in one shared world.

projects.name: Legends of Future Past
projects.description: An award-winning 1992 online text adventure from CompuServe, lost when it shut down in 1999 and rebuilt by its original creator from the surviving game scripts. Free to play in your browser.
projects.longDescription:
Legends of Future Past was one of the first commercial online multiplayer games, a text world (a MUD) set in the Shattered Realms of Andor with eight races, five schools of magic, psionic combat and over two thousand rooms. Computer Gaming World gave it a Special Award for Artistic Excellence in 1993.

The original engine's source code was lost, but former Game Masters had kept the script files that define every room, item, monster and quest. The new engine runs those original scripts, so the world is the real one. The server is free to play, and you can host your own copy.
projects.builtWithAI: Jon Radoff, who made the original game in 1992, says in the README that he used Claude Code to reconstruct it from the old script files, manuals and captured play sessions, in a weekend of agentic engineering. Checked 2026-11-22: all 120 commits are co-authored by Claude.

whatPeopleSay.summary: The AI-assisted revival got notable attention in Chinese tech and games media, which framed it as a 1990s online game brought back in a weekend with Claude. A 17173 writer who played it said the game beat their expectations and felt immersive despite being text only, though the lack of Chinese support was a hurdle. Former players commenting on the maker's write-up were mostly nostalgic and grateful, with one doubting the 'one weekend' framing.

Reviewer found the text-only game surprisingly immersive with plenty of content
Seen as a striking example of AI-assisted software preservation

projects.name: SkySend
projects.description: End-to-end encrypted file and note sharing you can host yourself: files are encrypted in the browser, links can expire or burn after reading, and no accounts are needed.
projects.longDescription:
Everything is encrypted with AES-256-GCM in the browser before it leaves the device, and the key travels in the part of the share link that browsers never send to the server. You can share files, whole folders, and notes with text, passwords, code or SSH keys, set expiry times and download limits, add a password, or send someone an upload link.

It runs as one Docker container with SQLite, stores files locally or in any S3-compatible bucket, and has a command-line tool. You can host your own or use a public instance. It was inspired by Mozilla Send and PrivateBin.

projects.name: DBackup
projects.alternative: Alternative to hosted database backup services
projects.description: Self-hosted backup automation for databases and files: scheduled, encrypted, compressed backups to the storage you choose, with restores in a few clicks.
projects.longDescription:
DBackup backs up 10 kinds of database (MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server, MongoDB, Redis, Firebird and more, directly or over SSH) together with the files that belong to them, then sends them to 13 kinds of storage such as S3, cloud drives, SFTP, SMB and WebDAV. It does incremental backups with daily, weekly, monthly and yearly retention, and can restore a whole database or a single file.

It runs as one Docker container. Backups are standard dumps and TAR archives encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and a Recovery Kit decrypts them without DBackup. It has SSO, permissions, 2FA, passkeys and an audit log for teams.

projects.name: ROM Librarian
projects.description: A desktop app for tidying retro game ROM collections: batch rename with No-Intro DATs, compress to ZIP or 7z, convert disc images to CHD and keep EmulationStation lists in sync.
projects.longDescription:
ROM Librarian has tabs for each cleanup job. Rename uses regular expressions and presets to strip region and dump tags, with a live preview and undo. DAT Rename matches files (even inside ZIPs) against No-Intro DAT files by CRC32, MD5 and SHA1. Compression batch-packs or unpacks ZIP and 7z, and Conversion turns CUE/BIN and ISO disc images into compressed CHD files for MAME and RetroArch.

Renames also update EmulationStation/RetroPie gamelist.xml files and the CUE sheets that point at BIN files. The Windows build is a portable zip with no Python needed; Linux runs it from source and has a command-line mode. It is for organizing games you own.

Emberwick is an original fantasy adventure: explore a 3D world from above, talk to characters, take on quests with companions and follow its plot. It also has a level editor. It runs in a desktop browser.

projects.builtWithAI: Simon Willison built it in the Claude chat app and wrote that everything in the game, "the graphics, the plot, the characters, the music, the dialog", came from the model (simonwillison.net, 2026-10-28).

projects.name: Quarter Sun Cove
projects.description: A cozy isometric farming game in the browser: grow pumpkins, tend your farm and meet a town of animal characters. Free to play, nothing to install.
projects.longDescription:
Quarter Sun Cove (first called Pumpkin Farmer) is a relaxed farming sim seen from an isometric view. You plant and grow pumpkins and get to know the animal characters who live around the cove. Its maker set out to make something original rather than an imitation of an existing farming game.

The written spec it was built from is published on GitHub, and the story of how it was made is on simonwillison.net.
projects.builtWithAI: Simon Willison wrote that he had Claude Opus 5.5 work for nearly two days building it from his spec (simonwillison.net, 2026-10-28).

projects.name: Starfall
projects.description: A 3D space real-time strategy game in the browser: build and command fleets from scouts to a two-kilometre mothership in full 3D, against a computer opponent.
projects.longDescription:
Starfall has thirteen ship classes, true 3D movement with a move disc for setting altitude, formations, stances and control groups, plus production, research, resource harvesting and an AI opponent. Every hull, planet, nebula and effect is generated in code at runtime, so there are no image files at all; the only bought-in assets are free (CC0) sounds and music.

It is an original game in the style of the classic 3D space strategy games, not a copy: it uses none of their art, sound, code or names. It needs a desktop browser with WebGL 2.

projects.name: SetShot
projects.alternative: Alternative to keeping notes on your Mac's settings by hand
projects.description: A Mac app that snapshots hundreds of macOS settings and compares two snapshots, so you can see exactly what an update, an installer or you changed, explained in plain English.
projects.longDescription:
Take a snapshot, change something (apply a macOS update, install software, adjust preferences), then take another. SetShot lists the recognized changes with a plain-English description, where to find each one in System Settings and, where possible, an Open in Settings button. Unrecognized changes show the raw name and old and new values, and can be submitted to grow its knowledge base.

A journal keeps a searchable history of every change, snapshots can run on a schedule in the background, and you can compare against built-in baselines of fresh macOS 15, 26 and 27 installs to export everything you've changed. It never changes settings itself, and snapshots stay on your Mac. Runs on macOS 13 Ventura and later.

projects.name: Parenthèse

Each person in the tree can hold photos, videos, audio recordings, documents and GPS tracks, and you can draw, add stickers or place photos anywhere on the tree. Relatives who get the link and password look around without an account and can suggest additions, which the owner can apply straight away or review first. GEDCOM import and export lets you move from or to other genealogy programs.

There is a hosted version at app.parenthese.io (with a demo that needs no account) and a Docker setup for running your own copy on a server or NAS. The interface is in English, French and German. The code is source-available under a non-commercial licence, not an OSI open source licence.

Mailflare gives you personal or shared mailboxes on custom domains, routing rules to store, forward, reject or sort mail, a calendar with time zones and email invitations, a public booking page, and a Drive for storing and sharing files. Built-in AI agents can search mail, draft replies and manage events. You can import mail from IMAP, Gmail Takeout, .eml and .mbox files, and the interface comes in 34 languages.

It deploys to Cloudflare Workers with one button or runs as a single Docker container, with a choice of databases (Cloudflare D1, PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite and others) and storage (R2, B2 or S3). projects.description: A flight simulator in the browser over real satellite imagery of Dallas-Fort Worth: fly a Boeing 737, a Cessna 172 or an F-16 in today's real weather and get every landing graded.
projects.longDescription:
It is a six-degrees-of-freedom flight model flown over the whole Dallas-Fort Worth area: land a 737 on DFW 35C, take an F-16 past Reunion Tower, or fly the approach into Love Field in a Cessna. projects.name: Sill
projects.alternative: Alternative to Sidecar and Duet Display
projects.description: Shows any Mac window, or the whole desktop, on your iPhone or iPad, where you use it with touch, a trackpad, keys or Apple Pencil. No account and no server in between.
projects.longDescription:
Sill for Mac sits in the menu bar and streams the window you pick, or the whole desktop, to the free Sill app on your iPhone or iPad as HEVC video over an encrypted connection. Taps, scrolls, three-finger gestures, keys and Apple Pencil go back to the Mac, the app's menus show up on the device, text can be shared through the clipboard both ways, and Mac sound can play along (a beta). A virtual display keeps the streamed window updating even when other windows cover it.

Devices connect on the same network, over a USB cable, with a direct Wi-Fi link when there is no shared network, or from away through your own VPN such as Tailscale. You pair each device once. It needs macOS 14 or later (Apple silicon or Intel) and iOS or iPadOS 17 or later. The Mac app is a free notarized download (or brew install --cask saffsanity/sill/sill) and the iPhone and iPad app is free on the App Store.

projects.name: Dimble
projects.description: A native menu bar manager for macOS 27 that hides the icons you don't need and brings them back on a hover, click or shortcut, or in a panel.
projects.longDescription:
Dimble sorts menu bar icons into Visible, Hidden and Always Hidden. You arrange them in a layout editor with real icon previews or by Command-dragging in the bar, and hidden icons come back on a hover, a click, a keyboard shortcut, or as tiles in a panel under the menu bar. Menu bar search (Option-Command-K) opens any icon's menu by name, and it can keep Live Activities visible, set behaviour per display, tighten icon spacing and add separators, app launchers and stand-ins for system items such as media controls and AirDrop.

It needs macOS 27, because it drives the native hiding built into the rebuilt macOS 27 menu bar through a private Apple framework, so a macOS update could break hiding. It asks for Accessibility (Screen Recording is optional, for animations), has no account or analytics, and installs from a notarized DMG or with brew install --cask dimble. It was called Pelmet until version 0.3.1 and is still in beta.

projects.name: WallpaperMachine
projects.description: Plays Wallpaper Engine scene, video and web wallpapers from the Steam Workshop as live wallpapers on a Mac, plus your own videos and pictures.
projects.longDescription:
Wallpaper Engine is Windows-only. WallpaperMachine is an independent Mac app, not affiliated with Wallpaper Engine or Valve, that plays its wallpapers with its own Metal renderer. You can browse the Steam Workshop inside the app without signing in, but downloading Workshop wallpapers needs a Steam account that owns Wallpaper Engine (Steam checks this), and scene wallpapers also need shared resources from a Wallpaper Engine you have bought. The app bundles neither. Without Wallpaper Engine you can still use the bundled video wallpaper, your own videos and pictures, and pixiv illustrations. Compatibility varies by wallpaper.

Each display can have its own wallpaper, and there are playlists, schedules, audio-reactive wallpapers, desktop widgets such as clocks and calendars, Shortcuts support and battery rules that lower quality or pause playback. It needs a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later, and installs from a free DMG or with brew install --cask wallpapermachine. A paid Priority Support option exists but unlocks no features.

projects.name: Prism Download Manager
projects.description: A download manager that splits files into up to 32 connections, resumes after crashes, and grabs videos, music and torrents. A browser extension hands downloads to it.
projects.longDescription:
Prism splits each download across up to 32 connections, writes straight to the final file and resumes after a crash, sleep or a dropped connection, checking that the file on the server has not changed. An extension for Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi and Firefox passes downloads to it, and it handles HTTP, FTP, HLS and DASH streams, BitTorrent and magnet links. Video and audio from YouTube and the other sites yt-dlp supports can be saved as MP4 or MP3, and it can fetch AI models from Hugging Face.

There are queues with schedules and speed limits, categories, batch downloads, a site grabber, a clipboard monitor and a mini window. Installers are for Windows 10 and 11, macOS 11 or later (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (deb, rpm, AppImage). They are not code-signed, so Windows and macOS warn on first start. No ads, account or telemetry.

projects.name: Screendrop
projects.alternative: Alternative to CleanShot X and Loom
projects.description: A native Mac app for screenshots and screen recordings, with an editor for both and optional Loom-style share links you host yourself.
projects.longDescription:
Screendrop lives in the Mac menu bar and captures a display, a window or an area, with a hotkey for each plus one that copies on-screen text with OCR. New captures land in a floating stack where you can copy, pin, annotate or upload them, and a Library window keeps every screenshot and recording in one place. The annotation editor is non-destructive, with arrows, shapes, text, smart redaction, crops, backgrounds and borders you can change later.

Recordings keep the screen, camera, cursor, clicks, keystrokes and audio as separate tracks, so you can add zooms, a smoother cursor, keystroke captions, camera layouts, cuts, speed changes and on-device captions after the fact. There is also a teleprompter that follows your voice. Sharing is optional and runs on your own Cloudflare account. It needs macOS 26.4 or newer, installs from a DMG or Homebrew, and the maker warns it is under active development with occasional breaking changes.

Screenshots open in an annotation editor with arrows, shapes, text, highlighter, numbered markers, pixelate and crop, and a beautify mode adds a background, padding, rounded corners and a shadow. projects.name: Reelbird
projects.alternative: Alternative to Loom and Screen Studio
projects.description: A Mac screen recorder that copies a share link the moment you stop, then lets you add auto-zoom, a smooth cursor and captions under the same link.
projects.longDescription:
Reelbird records a display, a window or an area, with camera, microphone and system audio on separate tracks. With sharing on, it uploads while you record and puts the link on your clipboard when you stop. Later you can open the same take, where it has already planned zooms on your clicks and typing, smoothed the cursor and levelled your voice, then trim, blur sensitive text, add captions or a background and update the video behind the existing link. It can also turn a recording into a step-by-step guide.

The app itself is free, with no account and no telemetry, and links can point at your own storage bucket such as Cloudflare R2. If you'd rather not set one up, the optional paid Reelbird Pro plan ($5 a month) hosts your links and adds viewer stats. projects.name: Compositor
projects.description: A free, native Mac image editor built around a Photoshop-style workflow, with layers, masks, adjustment layers, selections, retouching tools and filters.
projects.longDescription:
Compositor is made for compositing and photo touch-up the way Photoshop users already work: layers and folders with blend modes, layer masks and clipping masks, adjustment and filter layers, layer effects like drop shadow and glow, and non-destructive transforms. Selections include marquee, lasso, magic wand and Select Subject, and there are Spot Healing, Clone Stamp, brush, gradient, shape and type tools, a Camera Raw style panel, Content-Aware Fill and background removal. Shortcuts follow Photoshop's and can be remapped.

It opens JPEG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF, WebP, SVG, PDF, GIF, camera RAW and 8-bit RGB Photoshop PSD and PSB files, keeping folders, masks and simple text editable, and exports PNG, JPEG, PDF and animated GIF. It needs macOS 26 or later on an Apple silicon Mac. Download it from the site or GitHub, or install it with Homebrew (brew install --cask robbietilton-compositor).

projects.name: Rembrandt
projects.description: A free RAW photo editor and library with masks, healing, presets and on-device AI, where you can also describe edits in plain words. No account or subscription.
projects.longDescription:
Rembrandt develops RAW files from over 1,000 cameras and covers the everyday Lightroom work: tone and colour sliders, curves and grading, masks (brush, gradients, AI subject, sky, depth and people), healing and removal, lens corrections, presets and film looks, HDR, panorama and focus-stack merges, AI denoise and super resolution, and a photo library with albums and search. You can type or say edits like "warmer and a bit brighter" and watch the sliders move, using a small language model that runs on your computer.

Edits are saved as standard XMP sidecars next to your photos, so your originals are never changed and other editors can read the edits. There are installers for macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), Windows and Linux, or you can run it as a small server on the computer that holds your photos and edit in any browser. AI features can be switched off entirely. The builds are not code-signed yet, and the project warns that its editing engine is still changing between versions.

projects.description: A team workspace with pages, databases, whiteboards and a daily journal, edited together live. Host it yourself in one Docker container or use the hosted version.

projects.name: layerling
projects.description: Easy 3D design for people with a 3D printer: drop shapes on a plate, turn shapes into holes, round edges and export for your slicer. Runs in the browser with no account.
projects.longDescription:
layerling works the way Tinkercad does (a build plate, solid shapes and hole shapes, group, bundle, Alt-drag to copy) and then goes further: chamfers and fillets on any edge, hollowing to an even wall, splitting, sketches you can extrude or revolve, threads, gears, patterns, hole grids and holes for heat-set inserts. It knows the plate size of more than 230 printers, marks overhangs, runs a print check for thin walls and floating parts, and exports STL, 3MF, OBJ and STEP. It imports STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP, SVG and DXF.

There is nothing to sign up for: designs stay in your browser unless you save them as a project file. You can install it as an app that starts without internet, or host your own copy with Docker on a PC, NAS or home server. An optional MCP server lets an AI client such as Claude or Codex build in the open editor while you watch. It is not a full CAD package: there is no parametric timeline and no assemblies.

projects.name: PlayTranslate
projects.alternative: Alternative to Google Lens screen translation
projects.description: Translates the text on your Android screen in games, visual novels and manga with one tap, or automatically as dialogue changes. Works offline and helps you learn with word lookup and Anki cards.
projects.longDescription:
PlayTranslate reads the text on your screen and translates it over the game you are playing. Tap once to translate, or turn on auto mode and it follows the dialogue. You can crop to just the dialogue box, hover a lens over a word for its dictionary entry, show furigana or pinyin above the text, hear it read aloud, and point the camera at real-world text. It reads 26 languages and translates into 59, with offline OCR and dictionaries; online services such as DeepL or your own AI key are optional.

For learners it saves sentences to AnkiDroid with the translation, a screenshot and even recorded game audio, and it works with Yomitan dictionaries. It needs Android 10 or later and is installed from an APK on GitHub, not the Play Store, so Play Protect may warn and some features need accessibility permission. Dual-screen handhelds and split screen are supported.

projects.name: OnAir
projects.description: Turns a cheap software-defined radio into a receiver for digital TV, DAB radio, aircraft, ships, weather satellites, pagers and much more, with the spectrum and decoded data in one app.
projects.longDescription:
Plug in an RTL-SDR, HackRF, Airspy, SDRplay, LimeSDR, Pluto or one of many other radios, pick a mode and press Start. OnAir has close to 400 receive modes: digital TV (DVB-T/T2, ATSC, ISDB-T) with a live player, DAB+ and FM with RDS, ADS-B aircraft and AIS ships on a map, NOAA and Meteor weather satellite pictures, DMR, P25 and TETRA, pagers, FT8 and other ham modes, and sensors. It shows the spectrum, waterfall, constellations and a signal quality score, with auto-tune, gain help and a channel scanner. No radio yet? A built-in tour plays a demo signal.

Installers are on GitHub for macOS 15 or later (Apple silicon or Intel, not signed), 64-bit Windows 10 and 11, Linux (x86-64 and arm64) and Android 9 or later (receive only). Windows users need the WinUSB driver for HackRF, RTL-SDR and Airspy radios. Patented voice codecs are not included. Many newer decoders have been tested only on generated signals, so some may not work on the air yet.

projects.name: Parrot
projects.description: A Mac meeting recorder that transcribes any call on your own computer, with no bot joining. An optional assistant suggests answers from your documents during the call.
projects.longDescription:
Parrot records your Mac's system audio and your microphone as two tracks, so it works with Zoom, Google Meet, Teams or anything else your Mac can hear, and no bot joins the call. Transcription runs on the Mac with Whisper or Parakeet, it tells speakers apart, and afterwards it writes a report with a summary, objections, talk balance and the next steps people promised. You can search all your past calls and ask questions about them.

The live assistant is optional. You choose what powers it: Claude with your own API key, any OpenAI-compatible server, or a local model through Ollama, which keeps everything offline and free. You can add PDFs or notes, and it suggests answers from them while the other side is still talking. Parrot needs macOS 14 or later on an Apple silicon Mac. Releases are still marked as pre-releases, and the maker says some bugs remain.

projects.name: Nightwatch
projects.description: A menu-bar app for stargazers that finds tonight's clear window, ranks what you can see or photograph, and alerts you when it's worth setting up.
projects.longDescription:
Nightwatch sits in the Mac menu bar and checks the forecast every 30 minutes, using Apple Weather or Open-Meteo for cloud plus 7Timer for seeing and transparency. An hour before sunset it sends one alert if there's a long enough clear run in full darkness, along with a second forecast's opinion. It also shows a sky score, a plan for tonight with the best time for each target, the week ahead, events like meteor showers and ISS passes, and darker sites nearby.

You can tell it how much sky your trees and houses block in each direction, or measure that from a phone photo, and it only suggests targets that clear it. It knows your telescope or smart scope and suggests filters, exposures and frame counts. The Mac download needs macOS 14 or later on Apple silicon, and the app is also free on the App Store for Mac, iPhone and iPad.

projects.name: Seal
projects.alternative: Alternative to Google Inactive Account Manager
projects.description: An iPhone app for writing sealed letters and passwords that open for the people you choose if you stop checking in. Everything is encrypted on your phone.
projects.longDescription:
You write one envelope per person: a letter, photos, a voice message, a video, files and secrets like passwords. A few trusted people each hold a piece of the key, added in person. If you don't open the app for a set time (90 days by default), one of them can start a claim, you get daily warnings for weeks, and only then can enough key holders release the envelopes. Each one opens only for the person it was written for, and one tap from you stops the process at any point.

The envelopes are encrypted on the phone before they're stored in iCloud, and there's no password or email account, just a passkey or a security key. The app is for iPhone and iPad on iOS 18 or later; recipients and key holders can open envelopes in a browser. It's free to install, and the owner pays once to seal envelopes. The maker says the code hasn't been independently audited yet.

projects.name: Faro
projects.description: A desktop file client for SFTP, FTP, S3, WebDAV and cloud drives. Browse two places side by side, transfer and sync folders, and open an SSH terminal.
projects.longDescription:
Faro connects to SFTP, FTP and FTPS servers, S3-compatible storage such as AWS S3, Cloudflare R2 and Backblaze B2, WebDAV and Nextcloud, and cloud drives like Dropbox, OneDrive and Google Drive. You get two panes side by side with drag and drop, a transfer queue with pause, resume and bandwidth limits, folder syncs you can preview first, a disk usage view, and an SSH terminal in the same window. You can edit remote files in your own editor and import saved sites from FileZilla, PuTTY or your SSH config.

On Windows you can mount a server as a folder in Explorer, with files downloaded only when you open them. There's also a command-line tool and an optional bridge that lets a local AI agent use your open sessions, with each command needing your approval by default. Installers are available for Windows, macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Linux, but they aren't code-signed yet, so Windows and macOS show a warning on first launch.

projects.name: Tellyscope
projects.alternative: Alternative to Send Files to TV, ADB tools
projects.description: A phone app that looks after your Android TV, Google TV or Fire TV over Wi-Fi: remove bloatware, install apps, send files and use it as a remote. No root and no PC.
projects.longDescription:
Tellyscope connects to the TV over your Wi-Fi with ADB, the same debugging link developers use. Its debloat tool matches your TV to one of more than 330 tested lists and shows every app it will turn off before it does; built-in apps are only disabled, never uninstalled, and every change can be undone. It also installs APKs and split APK bundles from your phone, sends files to and from the TV, can set a launcher such as Projectivy as the home screen, and turns on ad-blocking Private DNS.

The phone doubles as a remote with a D-pad, typing and shortcuts to streaming apps, and an advanced monitor shows CPU, memory and network use per app. You need an Android phone on Android 8.0 or newer on the same Wi-Fi, and developer options turned on on the TV. Get the APK from GitHub, Obtainium or Orion Store; a Google Play version is in testing.

projects.name: ZenLink
projects.description: Shows your iPhone, iPad or Android phone on a Windows PC over USB or Wi-Fi, with sound, and lets you control it with mouse and keyboard. Android needs no app.
projects.longDescription:
ZenLink mirrors a phone or tablet in a window on Windows: 60 fps on iPhone and iPad and up to 120 fps on Android, with hardware decoding, synced sound and mouse and keyboard control. Android phones (5.0 or newer, sound from Android 11) connect over USB or Wi-Fi using the scrcpy server, with nothing to install on the phone. iPhones and iPads connect through Apple's driver (iOS 17 or newer with Developer Mode, for control) or through ZenLink Studio, which takes picture and sound over the cable or acts as an AirPlay receiver.

Extras include Alt+C to copy text off the phone screen with OCR, dropping files on the window to send them, launching Android apps in their own window, a stealth mode that dims the phone, and smooth capture in OBS for streamers. It needs 64-bit Windows 10 (1809) or Windows 11, and Apple Devices or iTunes for iPhones.

projects.name: HolyArrs
projects.alternative: Alternative to Sonarr, Radarr and Overseerr
projects.description: One self-hosted app that finds, requests, downloads and files your shows, movies and music for Plex, Jellyfin or Emby, in place of six separate *arr apps.
projects.longDescription:
HolyArrs does the jobs of Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Bazarr, Prowlarr and Seerr in one app with one login. You browse it like a streaming service, people in your household ask for a title, and it searches your indexers, picks a release by your rules, sends it to qBittorrent, SABnzbd or another downloader, fetches subtitles and files it into your library. It has a calendar, alerts to Discord, Telegram, ntfy and others, and can import an existing Sonarr, Radarr, Lidarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr or Seerr setup without changing it.

It runs as a small Docker container (about 16 MB) on amd64, arm64 or armv7, with an experimental Synology package too. Posters and search come from the maker's own metadata server, so no API keys are needed. The project went public in November 2026 and is still young.

The common worries are that it is very new and largely AI-written, that it depends on the maker's own metadata server, and that earlier attempts to merge the *arr apps faded away. Coverage so far is launch discussion and tutorials, not long-term use.

projects.name: BackupZit
projects.description: Self-hosted backup software run from one web console. It backs up PCs, servers, Proxmox, Hyper-V and VMware VMs, databases, NAS shares and Microsoft 365.
projects.longDescription:
A web console runs jobs for agents on Windows, Linux and Mac machines. It covers files, whole Windows disks and Linux systems with bare-metal restore, Proxmox VE, VMware ESXi and Hyper-V virtual machines (including instant recovery and automatic boot tests for Proxmox), SQL Server, PostgreSQL and MySQL databases, NAS shares and Microsoft 365 mail, OneDrive and SharePoint. Backups are deduplicated, compressed and encrypted, and can go to SFTP, S3, SMB, Azure, USB disks or an immutable hardened repository.

The console needs a small Linux VM (Debian, Ubuntu, AlmaLinux or Rocky) and comes as a ready-made VM image, an installer ISO, an install script or Docker. The Mac agent is Apple silicon only (macOS 13+) and backs up files. The first public release was in October 2026, and MaxZit sells optional support.

projects.name: PrintStash
projects.description: A self-hosted library for your 3D models that keeps each model's files, G-code revisions, slicer settings and print results together, and can send jobs to your printers.
projects.longDescription:
Upload models and archives or index a folder or NAS in place, then sort them into collections with tags, filters and saved views. It previews meshes and G-code layers, compares slicer settings between revisions, lets you mark the known-good one, and records print outcomes, time, cost and filament (with optional Spoolman). It runs as one Docker container on SQLite, with PostgreSQL, S3 storage and OIDC sign-in as options. Moonraker/Klipper is the main printer integration; Bambu LAN, PrusaLink, OctoPrint and Elegoo Centauri Carbon support is in beta.

Log sets quickly (shorthand like 100x8@9 works), with a rest timer, plate calculator, supersets and offline logging as an installable web app. Progress pages chart estimated 1RM and weekly volume per muscle, with a muscle heat map, records and a training calendar. projects.name: IMAGO
projects.description: A non-destructive photo editor for the photos on your Immich server or your phone, with light, colour, curves, masks and reusable recipes.
projects.longDescription:
IMAGO opens the photos on your own Immich server (version 2.6.0 or later, connected with an API key) or in your phone's gallery and edits them without touching the original: exposure, contrast, highlights and shadows, colour, a tone curve, an eight-band colour mixer, colour grading wheels, linear and radial masks, crop and straighten. Every edit is kept as a recipe you can change later, and exports go back to Immich at full resolution, stacked on the original.

It needs Android 12 or later and runs its adjustments on the device's GPU at 16 bits per channel. A composer turns photos into stories, posts and carousels. An optional account syncs recipes and presets between devices, but photos never sync and there are no ads or analytics. A Windows desktop app is in the same repo, but it has to be built from source; the site only links to Google Play. An optional supporter plan costs EUR 1 a month.

projects.description: A social media scheduler: write a post once, place it on a calendar and have it published to Mastodon, Bluesky, Instagram, TikTok, LinkedIn and more.

Postfalcon schedules posts for Mastodon, Bluesky, Facebook, Instagram, Threads, Telegram, YouTube, TikTok, Pinterest and LinkedIn (X too, if you pay for X's API). projects.alternative: Alternative to Mp3tag and MusicBrainz Picard
projects.description: A self-hosted music library manager you use from a browser: fix tags and cover art, match albums on MusicBrainz, rename and organise files, and file new downloads.
projects.longDescription:
Codetta runs next to your music and opens in any browser, including your phone. Edit tags for one track or a whole album with a preview before anything is written, match albums on MusicBrainz (with Discogs, Deezer and iTunes as fallbacks), rename and move files with a folder pattern, and point it at a downloads folder so new music is matched and filed. A library health check finds split albums, missing covers and duplicates, and every change can be undone from the activity log.

It handles FLAC, MP3, M4A, OGG, WAV, AIFF, WMA and more, and tells Navidrome, Jellyfin, Emby, Plex and Lidarr to rescan after changes. It runs as a small Docker container (Intel/AMD or ARM, Raspberry Pi 4 and up), or on a Linux or Mac computer via pipx (Python 3.14) or snap. It is still labelled beta, so keep a backup of your music.

projects.name: Ferry
projects.description: A small server on your home network that passes text, links and files between your phone and computers, with a shared timeline of everything each device sent.
projects.longDescription:
Ferry looks like a chat with yourself: paste a link, a shell command, a photo or a file on one device and it lands in a timeline every joined device can read, with a one-tap copy button. Files up to 64 MB are stored as uploaded, without re-encoding. There is no account; a new device joins by scanning a QR code, optionally gated by a shared password, and can be revoked later. Any message can be recalled from the server.

It runs as one Go server with SQLite, usually via Docker Compose on an always-on amd64 or arm64 machine, and is meant to stay on a trusted private network over plain HTTP, not the public internet. Any browser works as a client; optional native apps exist for Android 8+ (APK in the releases) and iOS 26+ (FerryDrop on the App Store). There is no automatic discovery or background clipboard sync.

projects.name: Hack://TheSystem
projects.description: A short, unsettling text-based horror game in your browser: type commands to break through four security layers of a rogue AI before its trace finds you, then face a boss.
projects.longDescription:
You sit at a hacker terminal and type commands to work through four puzzle stages, with Matrix-style effects, glitches and a trace meter that fills as you go. A boss stage, where you type the packets it throws at you before they reach your firewall, was added in an update on 24 October 2026; the maker admits it is hard.

projects.name: Zigzag
projects.description: A small, native Mac browser for people leaving Arc, with spaces, pinned tabs and split view. It runs on Safari's WebKit engine rather than Chromium, yet installs Chrome Web Store extensions.
projects.longDescription:
Zigzag keeps tabs in a sidebar grouped into spaces, each with its own color, pinned tabs and folders, plus favorites, profiles, a command bar, split view for up to four pages and a small pop-up window for quick links like Little Arc. Importing from Arc brings over spaces, pinned tabs, favorites, history, passwords and sign-ins, and it can also import from Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Zen and others.

Unlike most Arc replacements it is not built on Chromium: it's a Swift app on the WebKit engine that ships with macOS, about 35 MB installed, so engine security fixes come with macOS updates. Chrome extensions such as 1Password and Bitwarden install from the Chrome Web Store, though a few Chrome extension APIs are still missing. It has a built-in ad blocker, cookie banner refusal and dark pages, with no account or telemetry. It needs macOS 15.4 or later and has no sync between Macs yet.
projects.builtWithAI: The maker wrote on Show HN (2026-11-14): "Claude writes most of the code, but I am the one reviewing the quality, the functions and the UI/UX decisions." Few commits carry the trailer: checked 2026-11-24, 76 of 4,972 commits are co-authored by Claude.

projects.name: Mila
projects.description: A Mac app that records meetings, dictation and voice memos and transcribes them on the device, in English or Hebrew, with speaker labels and optional summaries.
projects.longDescription:
Mila records your microphone, the audio of one app such as Zoom, Slack or Google Meet in Chrome, or both together for meetings, with no virtual audio device to install. It transcribes with Whisper through whisper.cpp on the Mac's GPU, labels who said what and remembers speaker names, and exports SRT subtitles. Global shortcuts dictate English or Hebrew into any app, and voice memos synced from your iPhone are transcribed automatically. Titles and summaries can come from an AI tool you already use, and are off until you turn them on.

It needs macOS 14 or later; an Apple silicon Mac with 16 GB of memory is recommended, and the two default models take about 4.6 GB. Companies can instead point every Mac at their own transcription server and roll out settings through MDM or a shared config file.

projects.name: Bambu Bar
projects.description: Keeps your Bambu Lab 3D printer's progress and time left in the Mac menu bar or Windows tray, with temperatures, filament, the camera and print controls a click away.
projects.longDescription:
Bambu Bar shows percent done and time left in the menu bar, and a click opens a panel with the job, its stage, nozzle, bed and chamber temperatures, AMS spools with grams left and printer errors in plain words. You can pause, resume or stop a print, change its speed, switch the chamber light and watch the printer's camera. It watches several printers at once, adds desktop widgets and sends notifications when a print finishes, fails or pauses.

It talks to the printers directly over your local network, with no account or cloud, and reads access codes from Bambu Studio or OrcaSlicer during setup. Print controls need the printer in LAN Only mode with Developer Mode on. The Mac app needs macOS 26 or later and the Windows app Windows 10 (1903) or 11. The GitHub build is free; a one-time $9.99 supporter licence adds automatic updates.

projects.name: MacMix
projects.description: A menu bar audio mixer for the Mac: set each app's volume, give apps their own EQ, and switch speakers, headphones and microphones in one click.
projects.longDescription:
MacMix adds the controls macOS leaves out. From a small panel in the menu bar you can turn one app down without touching the rest, boost a quiet app up to 200%, and have MacMix remember each app's level. It switches between outputs such as AirPods, speakers and AirPlay receivers, picks the microphone, and can set the volume of external monitors over DDC/CI.

Every feature is open source, including per-app EQ with presets, sending one app to several devices at once, scene presets and Bluetooth battery levels. If you build it yourself in Xcode, everything is unlocked. The signed, self-updating download is free for the basics, and those extra Studio features are a one-time purchase. It needs macOS Sonoma 14.4 or later and asks for System Audio Recording permission for per-app mixing; audio stays on your Mac.

projects.name: Mirli
projects.description: A local studio for AI audio: make sound effects, music, songs with lyrics and voices on your own GPU, then arrange them on a multi-track timeline.
projects.longDescription:
Mirli (formerly Soundbox) is aimed at sound for games, videos and stories more than at voice alone. Describe a sound effect or a piece of music and it generates it; give it a lyric sheet and it makes a song; type a script and it voices each line with saved or cloned voices. Everything lands on a multi-track timeline with lanes for narration, dialogue, music and effects, where you can mix down and export. It can also extend or cover a track and split audio into stems.

It runs open-weight models such as Stable Audio 3.0 and ACE-Step through its own native runtime, with no account, no credits and no Python setup, and works offline once a model is downloaded. Each model's licence and commercial-use terms are shown before you download it. An NVIDIA GPU is the main target; it also runs on the CPU, slowly, and the Mac installers are not yet confirmed with the main models. There is a local HTTP API and an MCP server so Claude Code or Cursor can add sounds to a project.

projects.name: Tolaria
projects.description: A desktop app for a Markdown knowledge base kept as plain files, where every vault is a git repo and notes get types and relationships. Set up for AI agents to work in the same vault.
projects.longDescription:
Tolaria keeps your notes as Markdown files with YAML frontmatter in an ordinary folder, and treats that folder as a git repository, so you get version history and can sync through any git remote with no account or Tolaria server. Unlike a plain Obsidian-style editor, it is opinionated about structure: notes have types (such as projects, people or essays) and relationships, and there is an inbox, saved views, a command palette and a Notion-like block editor. It also has setup paths for Claude Code, Codex CLI and Gemini CLI, so AI agents can read and edit the vault and show up as their own git authors.

The maker built it to run his own vault of more than 10,000 notes. Downloads are offered for Mac (Apple silicon and Intel, also via Homebrew), Windows and Linux (AppImage, DEB, RPM), and an iPhone and iPad version is in TestFlight beta. On first launch you can clone a getting-started vault that walks through the app.

projects.name: BrightBean Studio
projects.description: Social media management for agencies: separate client workspaces, approval steps with a client review link, a shared inbox for comments and DMs, and scheduling to 10+ networks. Free hosted or self-hosted.
projects.longDescription:
BrightBean Studio plans, schedules and publishes posts to Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Mastodon, Google Business Profile and DEV.to (X is not supported). It is built for people running many client accounts: unlimited organisations, workspaces and team members with roles, approval stages with comments, a no-account magic link so clients can approve posts, a unified inbox for comments, mentions, DMs and reviews, per-post analytics, a media library, a Kanban idea board and recurring posting slots on a calendar.

projects.name: TikZ Editor
projects.description: A visual editor for TikZ, the LaTeX drawing language. Drag shapes, arrows and labels on a canvas and your TikZ code updates as you go, keeping your own formatting.
projects.longDescription:
TikZ Editor shows your TikZ source next to the rendered figure and keeps the two in sync. You can open a single figure, a whole paper's .tex file or a Beamer presentation, then move, resize, align and group elements, draw nodes, arrows, curves, matrices and trees, and edit styles in an inspector. When you drag something, only the numbers in that coordinate change, so your line breaks and indentation stay as they were, and existing \foreach loops keep working. It needs no TeX install to show the figure, and it flags code errors as you type.

It runs in the browser at tikz.dev, as a desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux, and as a free iPad app. It exports SVG, PDF, PNG or standalone LaTeX, and imports SVG, Ipe and PowerPoint files. Very hacky TeX may not be read correctly, and pgfplots and some advanced constructs are not supported yet. The desktop app has an optional assistant that uses your ChatGPT account through Codex. There are no accounts or analytics.

projects.name: Minute
projects.description: A Mac meeting note-taker that works with no internet at all. It notices when a call starts, transcribes it live, then writes a summary, decisions and action items with a local model.
projects.longDescription:
Minute records your microphone and, if you allow it, the other people on the call, with no bot joining the meeting. It can spot when Zoom, Teams, Slack, FaceTime, Webex, Discord or a browser call starts and offer to record, then stop by itself when the call goes quiet or ends. Whisper writes the transcript as people talk, and when you stop, a local language model writes a summary, the decisions and action items you can tick off. You can ask questions about one meeting, label speakers by voice and have them recognised next time, search every transcript, and save each note to an Obsidian vault as Markdown.

Everything runs inside the app: there is no account, no analytics and no cloud AI service to plug in, and it only goes online to download models or check for updates. It is a quiet note-taker rather than a live call coach. Notes are plain files on your disk, and audio is deleted after 30 days by default. It needs macOS 11 or later (13 or later to record system audio), at least 8 GB of memory and about 3 GB of disk for the default models. Apple silicon is the tested target; an Intel build exists but is untested.

projects.name: Torched!
projects.description: A short browser cooking game set in a tiny Paris bistro: sweep a kitchen torch over desserts and fish until they turn gold, not black, while a feared food critic watches.
projects.longDescription:
You are the new cook at Chez Flambeau. Hold the mouse button or your finger to torch, keep the flame moving until the whole surface turns amber, then ring the bell to serve. Five nights bring crème brûlées with guests' wishes (extra dark, light, half and half), a side of salmon whose thin tail cooks faster, a lemon meringue tart, marshmallow squares that can catch fire, and a night in the dining car of a train where curves and brakes move the plate under your torch. After each night the critic's review appears as a newspaper clipping, read aloud, with zero to three stars.

A guest book unlocks special orders for eight regular guests, an endless mode keeps five tables going until you lose three, and there are nine stamps to collect. A night takes about three minutes, it works with mouse or touch, and your progress stays in your browser.

projects.name: Kara and the Primal Torch

projects.name: Coalheart
projects.description: A short turn-based puzzle game in your browser: a little coal creature carries the last fire through a cold temple, and the order you collect and spend that fire is the puzzle.
projects.longDescription:
Torches never refill and every room holds exactly the fire it needs. You bump a torch to take its fire, spend 3 to light a brazier that opens the gate with the same rune and 2 to burn away brambles, all while a gauge limits how much you can carry. If the fire left can no longer reach the stairs, the game tells you, and undo and restart are free.

There are 15 rooms in three chapters, each with a par for the fewest moves, and your best results are kept in the browser. It plays with arrow keys or WASD, or by tapping and swiping on a touch screen. The pixel art, fonts, music and sound are all made in code.

projects.name: Lightkeeper
projects.description: Keep a lighthouse through seven stormy nights. Ships can only plot a course across water your beam has lit, so you sweep and hold the light to guide them past the rocks.
projects.longDescription:
You aim the beam with the mouse, a finger or the keyboard. Holding it on a ship lets it chart a safe route to the harbour as far as the light reaches, a Flash lights the whole sea for a moment at the cost of oil, and three wrecks lose the night. Each night adds something new: fog banks, lightning, currents, wind, smugglers, supply ships and a kraken that rises under neglected ships.

Between nights, letters arrive from the people you saved and the harbour sells upgrades such as a faster mechanism, a Fresnel lens, a rescue boat and a fog siren. All seven nights take about 15 to 20 minutes, progress is saved in the browser, and it is best played in landscape with sound on. All the art is drawn in code in a woodcut style.
projects.builtWithAI: The maker says on the jam page: "One person, zero hand-written code. I designed the game and made every call; AI agents built the rest in 13 days." The game's credits read "Code, art and tools: written with Claude (Anthropic) in Claude Code", with music from Suno and sound effects from ElevenLabs (https://itch.io/jam/ai-jam-5/rate/5265063).

projects.name: Xs of Y
projects.description: An unfinished but playable terminal-style roguelike that names itself every run. Its magic is a small Lisp: runes stand for code, and you piece spells together.
projects.longDescription:
Every run gets a new title (such as Voids of Deferred Maintenance), a new quest and a new mapping of runes, which secretly stand for Lisp expressions you inscribe on weapons and armour. The dungeon fights back in more ordinary ways too: spiders web you, slimes split, trolls regenerate, fire spreads through grass, and you can shove monsters into lava or chasms. The maker names Brogue as the main inspiration for its look.

The maker says plainly that it is not finished: it is playable, but expect bugs and crashes, and the rune system has no documentation yet. It runs in the browser, or in a terminal on macOS and Linux via Homebrew (brew install nooga/tap/xsofy). It is written in let-go, the maker's own Clojure-like language.

projects.name: The Human Box
projects.alternative: Inspired by god games and civilization sandboxes
projects.description: A civilization sandbox where Stone Age tribes invent languages, religions and wars on their own across 45 eras. Watch, or play god with blessings and disasters.
projects.longDescription:
Autonomous people are born with traits from both parents, learn, form tribes, build homes and cities, trade, found religions, sign treaties and go to war, from the Stone Age through 45 eras into speculative far-future ones. Each person has their own thoughts, memories, family tree and words of their tribe's language, all written by the simulation itself rather than a language model. You can watch at up to 5000x speed, follow anyone, read the world's chronicles, or use about 160 god tools to answer prayers, reshape land and send plagues or disasters.

The simulation is Rust compiled to WebAssembly and runs on your own device with no sign-up; worlds save locally and can be exported. Desktop apps for Windows, Linux and Apple silicon Macs are on the releases page; they are not code-signed yet, so you have to get past the security warning.

projects.name: Bokken
projects.alternative: Inspired by physics-based sword fighting games
projects.description: A 2D physics fighting game where you carve your own weapons out of pixels, and their weight, balance, edges and grip decide how they fight.
projects.longDescription:
There are no weapon types: you carve wood with a sharp stone, hone edges, join pieces of different materials and set the grip, and the game works out how the result swings. You steer your arms directly to swing and thrust, break scenery and knock weapons out of enemies' hands while crossing an island past a bandit, a monk and an Oni to face a Master. Fires heal you, and weapons chip and break, so you keep rebuilding them. There are three modes: one-life Realism, a more forgiving Gamified mode with checkpoints, and Endless.

It is a one-week prototype made with Godot for an AI game jam (Jamference: AI Game Jam Hack 2, October 2026). It plays in the browser with keyboard and mouse, a gamepad or touch (landscape only on phones), and there are downloads for Windows and Linux. The crafting takes some learning; the in-game help (H) explains it.

projects.name: OpenWorld RPG
projects.description: A pixel-art open-world RPG in your browser with over a thousand maps, a main story, real-time combat, crafting, farming and building, plus the engine and editor it is made with.
projects.longDescription:
You set out on a pilgrimage across a world of villages, cities, wilderness and dungeons, with a main story, side quests and jobs, real-time combat with telegraphed boss attacks, crafting, farming and building on your own land. More than 1,600 characters have homes, jobs and daily routines, and trade and react to what they see. It is in English and Chinese, and a demo is playable on the website.

All the world's rules are data. Optionally, a language model (your own API key, or a local setup) can propose a new rule when you try something no rule covers; the engine tests it before using it. The game is fully playable without any model. The repo also contains the TypeScript engine and a map and quest editor, and the project is the research platform for a paper. Code is MIT, the project's own art is CC0, and it also uses the CC0 Ninja Adventure pack.

projects.name: Calino
projects.description: A calendar in your browser that connects to your own CalDAV or JMAP server, such as Nextcloud, Fastmail or Radicale. It handles events, tasks and journal notes, with no Calino account.
projects.longDescription:
Calino is a calendar app that runs in the browser and talks directly to the calendar server you already use: Nextcloud, Baikal, Radicale, Fastmail, iCloud or any other CalDAV server, and JMAP servers such as Stalwart. It has month, week, 3-day, day, agenda and year views, drag-and-drop editing, a command palette where you can type something like "coffee on wednesday at 12" to create an event, tasks with priorities and recurrence, journal entries in Markdown, contacts from CardDAV, colour-coded categories and light and dark themes.

There is no Calino account and no backend: your calendar data and settings stay in the browser, and it can be installed as a web app. Use the free hosted version at calino.io or run your own copy with Docker. Your server has to allow browser requests (CORS), or you can go through a proxy, including one the project hosts. An Android app is available as an APK from GitHub Releases, not from Google Play.

projects.name: Dorso
projects.alternative: Alternative to Upright and other posture apps
projects.description: A Mac menu bar app that watches your posture through the camera or AirPods and gradually blurs the screen when you slouch. Sit up straight and the blur clears.
projects.longDescription:
Dorso sits in the menu bar and checks how you are sitting. With the camera it uses Apple's Vision framework to follow the position of your head against a baseline you calibrate while sitting up straight; with AirPods Pro, Max or 3rd generation and later it reads the tilt of your head instead, so no camera is needed. When you slouch, the screen blurs a little, then more the worse it gets. You can pick a glow, border or solid warning instead, set a dead zone, delay and sensitivity, pause it when you're away from your desk, and see a daily posture score with a seven-day chart.

All processing happens on your Mac, with no account and no cloud. It needs macOS 13 Ventura or later (AirPods mode needs macOS 14). The signed and notarized download on GitHub and the Homebrew install are free; the same app is also sold on the Mac App Store as "Dorso - Posture Monitor" for $4.99. It was first released as Posturr.

projects.name: Readfine
projects.alternative: Alternative to Feedly and Tiny Tiny RSS
projects.description: An RSS reader for the web that puts the articles you care about first, merges the same story from several sites into one row, and can summarize articles with your own AI key.
projects.longDescription:
Readfine is a web feed reader in the spirit of Tiny Tiny RSS. Subscribe to RSS and Atom feeds or YouTube channels, scrape sites without a feed using a CSS selector, or save any link to read later. Every new article gets a relevance score against topics you list, without any AI, so the best ones come first, and when several feeds cover the same event they collapse into one row. Filters can label, star, mark read or archive articles using regex and AND/OR conditions. The reader pulls in the full article text, plays YouTube and Vimeo videos in place, and has two- or three-panel layouts, a proper phone layout, dark mode and keyboard shortcuts. OPML import works with Tiny Tiny RSS.

AI features are optional and use your own key: summaries, a chat about an article, and "Catch me up" digests, also by email on a schedule, with Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or a local model through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint such as Ollama. You can sign up for free at readfine.app (up to 150 feeds) or host it yourself with Docker Compose and PostgreSQL; the setup script needs Linux, macOS or WSL2.

projects.name: Pesto Clipboard
projects.description: A free menu bar clipboard manager for the Mac. It keeps a searchable history of text, images and files you copy, one shortcut away.
projects.longDescription:
Pesto Clipboard sits in the menu bar and remembers more than 500 things you have copied, including text, images and files. Press Cmd+Shift+V (or your own shortcut) to open the history, type to filter it, and paste an item with Return or by its number from 1 to 9. Shift+Return pastes without formatting.

It needs macOS 14 Sonoma or later and installs from a DMG or with Homebrew. History is kept in a local database on your Mac, and copies from password managers such as 1Password and Bitwarden are skipped by default. The app is not sandboxed and does not encrypt its history itself; it relies on FileVault for that.
