projects.name: Roxel
projects.description: A lightweight desktop voxel editor for building small 3D scenes out of cubes, with import and export for MagicaVoxel, Goxel, OBJ and glTF files.
projects.longDescription:
Roxel gives you a big open canvas and a small floating toolbar: brush, erase, recolor, eyedropper, shapes (boxes, spheres, cylinders, lines), selection with copy and paste, and a move tool. It comes with palettes such as PICO-8, Sweetie 16 and Endesga 32, lets you make your own, and has light and dark themes and a command palette with every shortcut.

It opens MagicaVoxel .vox, Qubicle .qb and Goxel .gox files, and exports to .vox, .gox, OBJ, glTF (ready for Unity or Godot), transparent PNG and SVG, plus a lit, framed "Roxel Shot" image for sharing. A separate rox command-line tool can render and convert models without the app. Builds for Windows, macOS and Linux are on GitHub and itch.io; they are not signed, so macOS and Windows warn on first launch.

projects.name: Podium
projects.description: An Android music player built around a click wheel, styled after classic iPods. Plays your own music library, with Cover Flow, synced lyrics and lots of finishes to choose from.
projects.longDescription:
Podium turns your phone into a pocket music player with a wheel: turn it to move through menus, press the centre to choose, and press Menu to go back, with a click under your thumb on every step. It plays your local library by album and artist, flips through albums in Cover Flow, shows time-synced lyrics word by word, and keeps playing in the background with lock-screen and Bluetooth controls. It can also search and stream music online through an unofficial YouTube Music client (NewPipeExtractor).

Much of the fun is in making it yours: six body finishes or any colour, display themes, 17 typefaces, glitter in the case, and stickers cut out of your own photos. There are no ads and no analytics. It needs Android 10 or later and is installed as an APK from GitHub, not from Google Play.

projects.name: desigma
projects.description: A free, offline interface design app written in Rust, with frames, auto layout, components, prototyping and live collaboration. It opens Figma files.

desigma covers the everyday Figma workflow in a native desktop app with no web view: frames with auto layout, components with variants and properties, variables with light and dark modes, vector editing, prototyping with Smart Animate, keyframe motion, whiteboards and slide decks. Dev mode shows measurements and generates code in CSS, Tailwind, SwiftUI, Jetpack Compose, React, Flutter or Vue. projects.name: Tungsten Edge
projects.alternative: Alternative to uBar and the macOS Dock
projects.description: A per-window taskbar for the Mac: every open window gets its own card at the bottom of the screen, one click away, the way the Windows taskbar works.

Instead of one icon per app like the Dock, Tungsten Edge shows a card for each window, so getting back to one particular Finder or browser window takes a single click. Windows that are minimized or hidden show a greyed title, single-window apps stay as compact icons, and rarely used apps can be stashed in a drawer at the right end. It also has pinned folders like Dock stacks, unread badges for messaging apps, edge auto-hide and a taskbar on every display.

It is a native Swift app for macOS 12 or later (Apple silicon and Intel) and needs Accessibility permission to manage windows. Ready-made builds are on the official website. The maker says it is free until version 1.0, after which it becomes a one-time purchase (the site gives US$24 outside China, with a 21-day free trial), and people who join the founding-user list before then keep it free.

projects.name: Chipload
projects.alternative: Alternative to Vectric VCarve and Carbide Create
projects.description: Free 2.5D CAM software for CNC routers and mills: bring in a DXF or SVG drawing (or draw in the app), set up cuts, simulate them in 3D and export checked G-code.
projects.longDescription:
Chipload turns drawings into toolpaths: profiles with tabs and dogbones, pockets with islands, V-carving (including text), chamfers, drilling and boring, fill patterns, mouldings, surfacing and 3D reliefs carved from an STL model or a depth-map picture. A material-removal simulation shows the cut in 3D with cycle time and chip load, it can nest many parts onto boards, and an independent checker reads every program for machine limits, rapids through the stock and other mistakes before the G-code is written.

The maker says its programs have cut wood on a GRBL router (a Shapeoko) but have not yet been tried on LinuxCNC or Mach3/4, or in inches, and asks people with real machines to test it, starting with an air cut. It is written in Rust, with downloads for Linux, Windows and macOS.

projects.name: rec-rs
projects.description: A simple, fast screen and camera recorder for the Mac, made for recording YouTube videos. It records screen, system audio, microphone and webcam into one file and can stream as well.
projects.longDescription:
rec-rs records the screen, system audio, microphone and webcam into a single .mov or .mp4 that opens in QuickTime, Final Cut, Premiere and DaVinci Resolve, or writes screen and camera as separate files in sync. The webcam overlay can be dragged anywhere and shaped as a circle, squircle or pill. projects.name: jOtter
projects.alternative: Alternative to Jupyter Notebook and JupyterLab
projects.description: A fast Jupyter notebook app for the terminal, with vim keys, inline plots and rendered LaTeX. It opens and saves real .ipynb files.

jOtter edits and runs .ipynb notebooks in a terminal and saves them byte for byte the way Jupyter does, so collaborators using JupyterLab never notice. It finds your project's venv, uv, conda or pixi environment on its own, and has atomic saves, autosave and crash recovery. Install it with cargo, uv (PyPI), Nix, or the .deb, .rpm and .apk packages and static Linux binary on each release.

projects.name: Natel
projects.description: A small web app for editing the contacts on your own CardDAV server (Baïkal, Radicale, Nextcloud and others) from any browser.
projects.longDescription:
If you keep your address book on a CardDAV server so it syncs to your phones and computers, Natel gives you a clean place to search, fix and organise those contacts in a browser, on a computer or a phone. It does contacts only: no calendars, tasks or mail, and it does not host address books itself.

It runs as one small Docker container that you point at your server (or without Docker), and you sign in with your CardDAV account. It keeps fields it does not show, warns you instead of overwriting a contact someone changed on another device, and keeps your password in memory only. There is a public demo with made-up contacts that reset on reload.

projects.name: Dalibre
projects.description: A calm, fast desktop e-book library that reads and writes your existing Calibre library. One small native app, no web view.
projects.longDescription:
Dalibre is a lighter front end for the book library Calibre already keeps: point it at a Calibre library folder (or let it find the one Calibre uses) and browse, search and organise your books, with the same files and database underneath so you can keep using Calibre alongside it. Twenty sleepy buds march along a winding 3D path, and you hand out skills so they get past gaps, walls and drops and reach home. It has a world map, three camera views, voiced lines and a see-through outline for buds hidden behind scenery.

It plays in a phone or desktop browser and can be installed from the browser menu to run full screen and offline. The source is public so it can be hosted, but no licence is granted to reuse it.

projects.name: Clanker Racing
projects.description: A chunky retro off-road racer in the browser: beat five rivals on about two dozen silly tracks, from a dirt canyon to Mars.
projects.longDescription:
Flat-shaded 240-line graphics, uneven terrain, no barriers and limited nitrous: you can drive off the track and explore, and take shortcuts if you dare. The five AI drivers use the same physics as you, brake for bends, take shortcuts, use nitrous on straights and, on harder settings, try to block and bump you. Tracks include a river crossing, a lava bridge, a frozen lake and Tranquility Base with Earthrise.

It is plain JavaScript and WebGL 1 with no libraries or server, so you can also download it and open index.html. Keyboard, mouse and gamepad work; phones technically work too.

projects.name: PaletteRider
projects.description: Ride a bicycle through famous paintings turned into small 3D towns, from Klee's Castle and Sun to Van Gogh's Café Terrace at Night.
projects.longDescription:
Each chapter turns a real artwork into a little city you ride through. In Klee's patchwork town you collect fallen suns and bring them to the castle; in Van Gogh's Arles you carry stars back to the glowing café and watch them return to the sky; in Monet's Giverny you gather flowers by the lily pond; and in Hodler's Jungfrau you ride the real Lauterbrunnen valley, built from map and elevation data.

Get your load home before dawn and land your jumps cleanly, or half of it slips away. The paintings are public-domain reproductions.

projects.name: Summer Festival
projects.description: Walk an anime-style seaside town on the night of its summer festival: scoop a goldfish, win the ring toss and stay for the fireworks.
projects.longDescription:
You play a girl in a summer yukata on a street of food and game stalls under paper lanterns. Scoop a goldfish, buy a candy apple, win the ring toss, pick a mask and light a lantern, and when all five are done the fireworks go up over the sea. There is no score, no timer and no way to fail.

The town is busy around you: groups of festival-goers stop to chat, stall keepers call out, a dog follows you for a while. Morning, day, sunset and night are a click away. It needs a WebGPU browser (current Chrome or Edge on a computer), a keyboard and mouse, and about 11 MB on first load. By the maker of Valley Ride.

projects.name: Per My Last Email
projects.alternative: Inspired by choice-driven story card games
projects.description: A satirical office survival game: get through 12 weeks under a workplace bully, keep receipts and decide whether to speak up.
projects.longDescription:
You work at the fictional Celestial Pte Ltd, and Marcus is making your life hard. Over 49 story events in four acts you juggle sanity, performance, reputation and allies, collect evidence in a log, and watch a hidden strikes meter. Eight endings wait at the end, with a gallery to collect them, plus a top-down stealth minigame.

A run takes about 15 minutes on a phone or computer. All the art is hand-written SVG, with no image files.

projects.name: Shanhe
projects.description: A turn-based 4X strategy game on the real terrain of East Asia, with fifty fictional nations and xiangqi-style pieces on a sand-table map.
projects.longDescription:
Fifty fictional nations follow real province-level borders across East Asia, Siberia and Southeast Asia, each taking its flavour from its place. A whole 150-turn game can already be played against the AI, with cities, combat, war and peace, a tech tree and three ways to win. Terrain comes from public elevation data and everything else is drawn by shaders, with no model or texture files.

It is early: policies, diplomacy, trade and national traits are still to come, and there is no hosted build yet, so you clone it and run it with Node 24. The interface is in Chinese and English.

projects.name: Abyssal Garden
projects.description: Swim through a dreamy underwater world of kelp forests, sunbeams, a sunken ship and manta rays, all in one 96 KB HTML file.
projects.longDescription:
Swim freely through towering kelp that sways in the current, light rays falling through a rippling surface onto the sand, a wooden shipwreck, a giant stone whale tail, rock arches and a purple grotto, while manta rays and schools of fish drift past. The soundscape of rumbles, distant whale calls and chimes is made up as you listen.

There are no images, models or sound files: it is all code in one file that works offline. It needs WebGPU, so use Chrome or Edge on a computer.

projects.name: Aurora Courier
projects.description: Carry glowing lanterns across the northern sky; every gold ring you fly through turns the whole world into one of 473 art styles.
projects.longDescription:
You fly a small courier ship through the northern lights, bringing lanterns to a mountain village before dawn. Each gold ring is a portal: sky, rocks, lights and even the music snap into a new style, from pixel art and woodblock prints to neon wireframes, oil paint and synthwave.

It is calm but quick, with two modes and four endings, cutscenes and procedural music. It is one HTML file with nothing to download or install.
